transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (Skyline Head of AI), Priya Patel (Eng Lead), Marcus Chen (DevOps), Evelyn Brooks (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick onboarding workshop to align on pilot goals, environment requirements (VPC/private deployment vs Dedicated), SSO and procurement timeline, and immediate next steps to get a pilot running for Skyline's claims summarization feature.

Topics covered:
- Pilot success metrics (latency targets, cost per inference, fidelity)
- Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
- Networking and data access (S3, sample datasets, ingress/egress)
- Compliance: SOC2, encryption, audit logs, and KMS integration
- Timeline and procurement checkpoints

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex here, Samira and Diego from Redwood.
[00:07] Jordan (Skyline): Hey hi, Jordan on my side, Priya, Marcus, Evelyn's on. Thank you.
[00:12] Alex: Cool. The plan for today is 45-ish minutes of tech + logistics and then we block 10 for next steps. If anyone needs a different focus say now.
[00:22] Priya (Skyline): We're hoping to validate latency and accuracy on the claims summarization flow, and also want to understand the networking work for private access.
[00:30] Samira (Redwood SE): Got it. We'll walk through three things: what the pilot will measure, the infra options with rough tradeoffs, and then immediate setup steps for credentials and sample data.
[00:42] Jordan: Quick note — procurement wants a clear SOW and a list of controls for SOC2. Evelyn will flag anything missing.
[00:50] Diego (Redwood CSM): Yeah, we'll include our SOC2 summary and a security checklist in the packet.
[00:56] Alex: Samira, can you start with a quick overview of Dedicated vs Private?
[01:02] Samira: Sure. So Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity in our cloud with dedicated pools only for Skyline — that gives predictable throughput and simpler onboarding. Private (VPC) means we place a deployment behind a customer-managed VPC, e.g., your AWS account, for additional network isolation — it's slightly more setup but needed for regulated data. Hosted API is the fastest to try but might not satisfy data residency or certain contract requirements.
[01:28] Priya: For our team, the requirement is that raw PII data doesn't leave our VPC. We're leaning Private, but we'd like to know the timeline.
[01:36] Samira: Typical Private onboarding is 3-4 weeks for an initial pilot if there's network support on your side — includes peering, NSG rules, and KMS key exchange. Dedicated can be faster since it's just redistributing models and configs — usually 1-2 weeks if you don't need VPC peering.
[01:52] Marcus (Skyline): For peering, we have a standard VPN + Transit Gateway setup. Would that be supported?
[01:58] Samira: Yes, TGW and VPC peering patterns are supported. We'll need your account IDs and a network egress IP. Marcus, can you share the diagram?
[02:06] Marcus: Yup, will share after.
[02:09] Jordan: On metrics, our product team wants <220ms median for a 512-token summary and cost per 1k requests to be under our budgeted target — I'll share the exact number in the follow-up.
[02:20] Alex: Good. We'll capture target SLOs in the SOW. For cost, Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization to hit cost targets — Samira will show an example later.
[02:30] Samira: Quick demo, I have a sample runbook — so if you imagine a 512 token typical input, with moderate batch sizes we can show either single model low-latency paths or batched throughput. Note: quantized variants trade off a small drop in fidelity.
[02:45] Priya: How do we measure fidelity regressions? We need thresholding and rollback.
[02:50] Samira: We tie monitoring to your evals — Redwood Console supports sets of prompt tests, and we can alert on regression. We also support automatic fallback to a higher-precision model if you hit a threshold.
[03:05] Jordan: That fallback path — is it instant? We can't have a 30-second blackout.
[03:10] Samira: Fallback is near-immediate for compatible variants; there's a tiny ramp to spin up capacity if the alternate model isn't warm, but we can pre-warm. We'll discuss warm pools if that's a hard SLO for you.
[03:22] Evelyn (Procurement): On purchase order and legal — what does the trial contract look like? We need an IP clause and data handling terms spelled out.
[03:30] Diego: We'll send a pilot SOW template that includes data handling, IP, and a 30-day pilot term by default. Legal can redline it; we have an enterprise addendum for private deployments.
[03:40] Evelyn: Great. Also need the SOC2 report — you mentioned a summary.
[03:44] Diego: I'll attach our SOC2 type 2 summary and the security checklist after the call.
[03:49] Alex: Marcus, let's talk nuts-and-bolts for access — S3 buckets, roles, and VPC endpoints.
[03:55] Marcus: We can expose a read-only bucket with sample claims. We prefer to avoid putting production PII into any external storage for the pilot.
[04:03] Samira: Totally makes sense. For the pilot we can run on a redacted dataset or on-prem samples through a secure channel. If you do S3, we recommend using a role-based cross-account access with least privilege and VPC endpoint.
[04:16] Priya: About KMS — we use a customer-managed KMS key. Will Redwood support that for Private?
[04:21] Samira: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments. We'll coordinate the key policy and a whitelist for the Redwood service principal.
[04:30] Jordan: Any special notes about KV cache or session state with our summaries? We have streaming and longer conversation contexts.
[04:37] Samira: The runtime supports KV caching; for long context we recommend an external cache if you need persistence beyond the model session. There can be cache encryption too.
[04:46] Alex: Quick question about observability — Diego, do you want to walk through Console features?
[04:50] Diego: Yeah. Console will show token-level cost, latency distributions, per-route dashboards, and alerts. You can plug in tracing hooks. We'll also set up a channel for post-mortem logs.
[05:02] Jordan: Is the console tenant-isolated for Private deployments?
[05:07] Diego: For Private we provide a control plane that can be integrated with your IDP; the Console view can be restricted to your org.
[05:12] Priya: For the pilot, we probably want a small Dedicated pool behind our VPC so we don't deal with capacity cold starts — is that possible?
[05:20] Samira: Yes, that hybrid is common: Dedicated GPU pool with network isolation. We'll call that Dedicated-in-VPC and it's basically Reserved capacity plus VPC placement. Setup complexity is higher but it meets SLOs.
[05:33] Marcus: Any pre-approved AMIs or agents we need to run in our account?
[05:37] Samira: No agents inside your account for the Dedicated model; for Private we may ask for a small bootstrap VM to handle networking handshakes, but we manage most service components. We'll document the steps.
[05:49] Jordan: Can we run an initial benchmark against our dataset?
[05:51] Alex: Yes — sample benchmark run is part of the pilot. Samira will configure the benchmark harness; we ask you to provide representative samples.
[05:58] Priya: Timeline question: if we start next week, when can we see results?
[06:02] Samira: If networking info and credentials arrive promptly, we can instrument a pilot in ~7-14 days and have baseline metrics in that window. Private may push to the 3-4 week mark.
[06:14] Evelyn: From procurement side, if we sign a POC SOW are there upfront fees?
[06:18] Alex: Pilots are typically credit-based; there might be a small onboarding fee for Private. We'll include that in the SOW options.
[06:26] Jordan: Any blockers on Redwood's side we should be aware of?
[06:29] Samira: No specific blockers; main dependency is receiving network details and a sample dataset. Also the SSO integration requires an SP metadata endpoint if you guys control the IdP.
[06:40] Marcus: We'll provide the account IDs and TGW architecture by Monday.
[06:44] Diego: Great. I'll open a shared Confluence page and invite you; that'll have the runbook, checklist, and ticket links.
[06:51] Alex: OK let's recap action items and next steps.
[06:54] Diego: Recap: Redwood to send SOW template, SOC2, onboarding checklist, and pricing options. Skyline to share network diagrams, account IDs, sample dataset redacted. Schedule the technical deep dive for Wednesday next week.
[07:07] Jordan: Sounds good. Evelyn: any final procurement asks?
[07:11] Evelyn: Just the SOW and an initial T&Cs summary. If you can get that by Monday that helps.
[07:16] Alex: We'll aim to send the packet by Monday EOD.
[07:19] Samira: I'll follow up with a short tech agenda for the deep dive and a baseline config recommendation for Dedicated-in-VPC.
[07:26] Priya: Thanks everyone — looking forward to the deep dive.
[07:29] Alex: Thanks all, we'll send notes and assign owners. Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription artifacts: occasional overlaps and filler words (uh, mm), some product names transcribed slightly off in auto transcript (e.g., "Dedicate" instead of "Dedicated"). Speaker labels partially normalized.
